title: Setting a wrong clock from TLS certificates
claim: Modeled on US10069839B2, filed February 11, 2016. A method comprising: noticing that secure connections fail because the device's clock is wrong; taking the time from the certificates and metadata that secure servers send; approximating the current time from several servers; and holding back sensitive data until the time has been approximated.

elements.element: Noticing that secure connections fail because the device's clock is wrong
elements.question: Did anyone describe a device noticing that its secure connections fail because its clock or system time is wrong?

elements.element: Taking the time from certificates and metadata sent by secure servers
elements.question: Did anyone describe a device taking the current time from the certificates or other metadata that secure servers send?

elements.element: Approximating the current time from several servers
elements.question: Did anyone describe a device approximating the current time from the time information of several secure servers?

elements.element: Holding back sensitive data until the time has been approximated
elements.question: Did anyone describe preventing applications from sending sensitive data until the device's time has been approximated?
